{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOUDROfM8AAAABiwuhEw", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4BlR_zzhMHUSo", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4BlR_z", "number": 409, "title": "Follow current focus during desktop dictation instead of stopping on focus changes", "body": "## Problem

Desktop voice typing currently binds the focused application, window and field when the recording starts. Moving focus to another field or application invalidates that binding, cancels the session and discards pending output. This makes ordinary workflows (dictating into several fields or switching applications while speaking) unnecessarily difficult.

The user explicitly wants the simpler keyboard-like behavior: **paste each committed text chunk into whatever is focused when the paste is performed; do not stop recording merely because focus changes.** Starting and stopping recording should be controlled by the user, not by focus.

Affected main revision: [aae215b](https://github.com/takahirox/my-audio-to-text/commit/aae215b3a832d6f9a1b07c72be8802f7b0d70201), after #407 / PR #408.
- [desktop/mac-target.m](https://github.com/takahirox/my-audio-to-text/blob/aae215b3a832d6f9a1b07c72be8802f7b0d70201/desktop/mac-target.m): session-bound focus, AX focus-change invalidation and dispatch checks.
- [desktop/session.js](https://github.com/takahirox/my-audio-to-text/blob/aae215b3a832d6f9a1b07c72be8802f7b0d70201/desktop/session.js): target binding at Start and cancellation on output errors.
- [desktop/x11-accessibility.py](https://github.com/takahirox/my-audio-to-text/blob/aae215b3a832d6f9a1b07c72be8802f7b0d70201/desktop/x11-accessibility.py): analogous session-bound target policy.
- [docs/desktop.md](https://github.com/takahirox/my-audio-to-text/blob/aae215b3a832d6f9a1b07c72be8802f7b0d70201/docs/desktop.md#focused-fields): currently instructs the user to stop before switching apps/fields.

## Expected outcome

### Follow current focus, without stopping recording

- On macOS, keep the clipboard + native Cmd+V method introduced by #408. Resolve the current foreground target at the time each queued committed TEXT chunk is actually dispatched. Do not bind the recording session to the app, window or field focused at Start or when recognition finished. Use the current OS focus and ordinary paste semantics; never force an earlier app or field to regain focus.
- Moving between fields within a window, between windows, or between applications must not stop, cancel or restart the recording or graph. Subsequent chunks naturally follow the new focus. Starting dictation does not require a particular editable field to remain focused. A focus change during model preparation, shortcut release, clipboard staging or between queued chunks is not a fatal error. If necessary, refresh the target immediately before dispatch; do not retry a Paste already dispatched.
- If focus is on a menu, a noneditable control, a known protected/password/read-only field, or there is temporarily no usable target, keep recording. Where native paste is appropriate, let the current application's normal handling accept or ignore it; otherwise skip that chunk without dispatch. Do not retain a backlog of chunks skipped due to an unavailable/protected target for later insertion into a different field. Resume ordinary delivery automatically on the next committed chunk after a usable target becomes focused. Missing Accessibility editing metadata alone is not grounds to skip or stop. Avoid intrusive warnings or new confirmation dialogs for normal focus changes.
- The user's intended behavior is that speech committed after a focus switch (including a chunk whose audio started before the switch) can be inserted at the new focus. This is intentional, not a wrong-target regression. An in-flight paste may still be affected by ordinary OS focus/clipboard timing; do not require atomic external edits or perfect focus synchronization. Keep the existing 250 ms settling/restore approach unless a concrete need justifies changing it.
- Keep explicit Stop, Cancel, Quit, runtime-error and OS-permission handling. Stop drains accepted output using the same current-focus rule; Cancel/Quit discard pending output and finish any necessary clipboard cleanup. Do not let stale callbacks from ended sessions insert text. Keep native secure-input protections, normal permissions, no automatic submit or arbitrary commands, serialized committed output, no blind retry of ambiguous delivery, and clipboard preservation/ownership guards from #407. A genuinely fatal runtime or permission failure may stop the session; ordinary focus changes and transient unavailable targets must not.
- Apply the same user-facing focus-following behavior to the existing Linux X11 path where supported, using its current AT-SPI insertion mechanism. Resolve the currently focused editable target at delivery time; unavailable/unsupported targets do not cancel recording. macOS is the primary implementation and validation target. Do not expand this into a Linux clipboard migration, full browser/Wayland support, or all-platform compatibility effort.
- Simplify the old session-long target binding, invalidation events, cancellation paths and tests where superseded. Retain only the session/lifecycle authorization and per-dispatch checks actually needed. No new target-lock toggle, per-app settings, allowlists, feature flags, or unrelated redesign. Preserve generic graph output, shared Pipeline and existing browser/extension behavior.

### Pre-merge acceptance (automated; no human gate)

- [ ] Deterministic tests demonstrate a single continuous session delivering ordered committed chunks to field A, then field B in the same app, then a different app/window, without stopping or restarting capture. Cover a focus switch while a chunk is queued or clipboard staging is underway; dispatch uses the current focus, not a stale session-start target.
- [ ] Tests demonstrate that an unavailable or known protected target does not cause cancellation, skipped chunks do not accumulate for replay, and later committed chunks can be delivered to a newly focused eligible target. Retain normal permissions and secure-input handling. Do not require positive AX editability metadata for macOS paste.
- [ ] Preserve relevant streaming clipboard serialization, restoration/ownership, Stop/Cancel/Quit, held modifier, no duplicate dispatch, provisional output exclusion and stale session regressions. Replace old tests that demand session cancellation on focus change; do not treat intentional current-focus delivery as an error. Keep tests at the lightest meaningful layer rather than exhaustively enumerating apps and OS races.
- [ ] Build and launch the macOS app; run `npm test` and applicable focused desktop tests. Update applicable X11 tests and validate where the existing environment permits. Native independent-app checks requiring unavailable OS permissions remain optional and must be reported honestly. No new authorized runner, exhaustive compatibility testing, or user/manual confirmation is required to merge or close.
- [ ] Update the desktop guide, relevant errors and PR description to explain current-focus delivery, the effect of switching focus mid-dictation, skipped/unavailable targets and ordinary clipboard timing limitations. Provide brief optional manual steps for dictating into two fields and two apps in one session, without stopping between them. Remove obsolete instructions to stop before changing focus. Run `git diff --check`.

## Required post-merge verification

None. Manual user testing remains optional.

## Context

Follow-up to #401, #403, #405 and #407 / PR #408. This Issue deliberately supersedes their earlier session-long focus-binding and focus-change cancellation requirements. The user wants ordinary current-focus text entry and explicit control of recording Start/Stop, not a locked target. Preserve the existing no-human-gate policy, [development flow](https://github.com/takahirox/my-audio-to-text/blob/main/docs/development-flow.md), [review guidelines](https://github.com/takahirox/my-audio-to-text/blob/main/docs/review-guidelines.md), and UI/UX principles.
